text.tspan: A low-fidelity end-to-end food-delivery experience that helps hungry people choose quickly, understand the total cost, and know
How can ordering feel fast without hiding
the details people need to trust the

g.text: Constraint: support a first-time order in under 4 minutes, with price
Start with the decision, not the interface.
Most orders begin with a craving, not a restaurant.
Delivery time and total cost drive the shortlist.
Scan relevant options without opening every menu.
See fees, ETA, and item requirements early.
Recover easily when an item or address changes.
Unexpected fees appear late in checkout.
Dense menus make dietary checks slow.
Lead with decision-making signals, not promotions.
Keep a persistent, itemized cost trail.
Make each delivery state specific and actionable.
“Show me what will arrive soon and
Get a reliable dinner to her apartment between calls; reorder favorites with minimal effort.
Filters by 30 min or less, checks ratings, compares the final total, saves vegetarian dishes.
Fees that change at checkout and menus with unclear dietary labels.
Parent of two · weekly family order
Build a family-friendly order, customize items safely, and time arrival around bedtime.
Browses by cuisine, reads item details, adds notes, and tracks every delivery milestone.
Losing cart edits, unclear substitutions, and a tracker that only says ‘on the way.’
One clear path from hunger to handoff.
Primary path · back/edit allowed before payment
↳ Recovery rule: preserve selections when users return from item details, cart, or checkout. If unavailable, explain why and offer the closest replacement.
Fees shown before you open a menu
Thick rice noodles, Chinese broccoli, egg...

text.tspan: updates stay attached to the CTA.

g.text: By placing this order, you agree to the terms
Siam Corner is preparing your order

text.tspan: ↳ Receipt, order number, ETA, and next

g.text: What shaped the wireframes—and what comes next.
Frame contexts, needs, and trust gaps.
Prioritize speed, price clarity, and certainty.
Observe behavior; revise hierarchy and copy.

text.tspan: Time-pressed diners need a fast way to compare, customize, and track delivery
because hidden costs and vague status updates make ordering feel risky.
…help people commit quickly while keeping total cost, timing, and order progress

g.text: Show delivery cost in results and an itemized estimate in cart.
Separate discovery, customization, review, and payment into clear checkpoints.
Keep cart state while people edit items, address, timing, or payment.
Pair every tracking state with an ETA, timestamp, or next action.
TARGET: 4/5 complete order walkthrough in <4 min
TARGET: users predict final total within $1
TARGET: 80% correctly explain status + next step
TEST: unavailable item, late courier, address edit
Ready for critique: validate the riskiest assumptions before increasing fidelity.
